text:
Alex: FYI — we've been seeing GPU pod evictions in us-west-2 since ~22:10 UTC. Several pods went Terminating and never came back up because CA couldn't provision new GPU nodes. Logs attached but short version below.

infra-bot: AUTOSCALER EVENT | 2025-11-03T22:12:40Z | Group=hosted-shared-gpu | Reason=NoCapacity | message=No capacity for requested instance types, quota/az limits hit.

Matt: Which nodepool exactly? hosted-shared or one of the dedicated pools? spot vs on-demand?

Alex: hosted-shared-gpu (spot-backed). Looks like multiple teams launched big batch jobs at once — there was no namespace GPU quota so they all requested GPUs.

Sana: Oof. Two quick levers: namespace-level resourceQuota (max gpus) + limitRange to avoid one team hogging. Also enforce priorityClass for infra-critical pods vs tenant jobs so PDBs + priority reduce user-facing evictions.

Matt: This is the classic dedicated vs hosted tradeoff. Dedicated pools avoid noisy neighbors but cost more (reserved capacity). We should define a policy: critical customers -> Dedicated with reserved nodes; non-critical -> hosted with limits and fair-queueing. How do we enforce assignment?

Alex: We can gate GPU requests with an admission webhook that checks a namespace tag/annotation. If not approved, reject GPU requests or redirect to a queued job API. But onboarding all existing namespaces will take time.

devops-oncall: Note: cluster-autoscaler had --max-node-provision-time=15m for those groups. With spot/interruptible instances and launch retries, 15m is too tight. Also scaleUpFromZero was disabled for the gpu nodegroups, so CA wouldn't scale from zero to satisfy pending pods.

Sana: Add taints+tolerations and nodeAffinity to pin dedicated pools (taint=dedicated=true:NoSchedule). That reduces cross-tenant interference. For critical inference services use PodDisruptionBudget + priorityClass so they aren't evicted during scale-down.

Matt: Operational idea: warm pool / pre-warmed nodes. Keep a tiny baseline of on nodes for hosted GPU pools to handle short bursts. For Dedicated customers we include warm capacity in the commit; for hosted we can charge a micro-fee or amortize across usage. This avoids expensive cold starts and failed launches.

Alex: Important networking note — we've seen fallback to other regions when capacity isn't available; causes big egress and latency spikes for customers. We should avoid cross-region fallback for stateful inference; prefer queuing until local capacity or explicit failover.

infra-bot: SCALE QUEUE | queued=3 pods | reason=AZCapacityLimitExceeded | group=hosted-shared-gpu

Sana: Proposed action items:
1) Create strict GPU resourceQuota for sandbox and default namespaces (max 1) and soft limits for team namespaces.
2) Infra to implement admission webhook to require a namespace annotation for GPU allocation.
3) Increase CA --max-node-provision-time to 30m and enable scaleUpFromZero for GPU node groups.
4) Evaluate a ~2-5 node warm pool for hosted GPUs and cost impact; finance to run calc.

Alex: Assigning: @Sana to draft the RFC for the webhook + namespace quotas, @Matt to run warm-pool cost calc and SLA impact. I'll attach the detailed logs and pending pod IDs.

Matt: Ack, starting cost calc now. Will ping infra with numbers. :+1:

Sana: I'll start the RFC and a short rollout plan (admission webhook + retroactive tagging script). Thanks everyone.
